title: TF contracts, image provenance and release guardrails for private deploys
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a pragmatic CI/CD guardrail set and Terraform module contract pattern for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: ensure reproducible artifact provenance, deterministic Helm upgrades, and safe rollouts when using GitOps (ArgoCD) and signed OCI images in environments with mixed connectivity (VPC, air-gapped customers).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments where Redwood pushes/orchestrates upgrades (dedicated operator path) or customers pull via ArgoCD + mirrored registries.
- We assume an OCI registry (customer-provided or Redwood-managed private registry mirror) that supports manifests and OCI refs.
- Image signing uses cosign with KMS (AWS KMS/HSM or customer HSM).
- Terraform modules manage infra primitives and produce a minimal set of outputs that the release pipeline consumes.

High-level goals:
- Every promoted release artifact must have a verifiable provenance bundle (image digest + cosign statement + build metadata).
- Terraform module interfaces explicitly return artifact_provenance and rollout_metadata so CI and ArgoCD can gate syncs deterministically.
- Upgrades must be expressible as phases (prepare -> promote -> validate -> finalize) and support fast rollbacks without state drift.
- Minimize manual intervention for routine upgrades; make manual steps explicit for high-risk operations.

Roles and responsibilities (quick):
- Eng-private-deployments: owns TF module contracts and CI gating logic.
- Solutions eng / SE: coordinates with customer registry/KMS setup and validates airgap promotion steps.
- Release eng: maintains ArgoCD app templates and pre-sync hooks.
- Customer infra (when applicable): enables registry mirror, provides KMS/HSM credentials, approves rollout policy.

Terraform module contract pattern (recommended):
- Each module that is part of the release path should expose clearly typed outputs used by the release system. Keep inputs minimal and stable.
- Required outputs (string values):
  - rollout_id: unique id for the deployment attempt (e.g. "rdw-roll-20241102-03")
  - artifact_digest: fully-qualified image digest (sha256:...)
  - artifact_reference: semantic ref that may include variant/quant (e.g. gcr.io/redwood/rlm:v2.3-q4)
  - provenance_blob_url: signed statement URL or S3/OCI attestation reference (if airgapped, may be a local file path policy)
  - preflight_checksum: checksum of the rendered helm manifests used for deterministic compares
- Optional outputs: db_migration_plan_id, operator_image_digest, sequester_key_id

Example TF snippet for module interface (pseudo-HCL as doc string):
  variable "app_image_ref" { type = string }
  module "service" {
    source = "git::ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/tf-modules.git//service-module?ref=main"
    app_image_ref = var.app_image_ref
  }
  output "artifact_digest" { value = module.service.artifact_digest }
  output "provenance_blob_url" { value = module.service.provenance_blob_url }

Contract notes / versioning rules:
- Semantic changes to module outputs are breaking; bump module major version and add migration notes.
- If a module needs to stop returning an output, add a compatibility shim for one release cycle.

Image provenance and signing flow (recommended):
1) Build -> produce image digest and SBOM (container-analysis) and a compact provenance statement (build id, git sha, builder image, timestamp).
2) Sign image with cosign using customer KMS or Redwood-managed KMS (for hosted mirrors). Store signature alongside manifest in registry and copy the provenance bundle to a signed S3 path (or offline bundle for airgap).
3) Generate a concise provenance index file that maps tag -> digest -> cosign signature -> sbom_url. This index is the single source-of-truth for the release pipeline.
4) CI attaches the provenance index URL into Terraform module input (or pushes to a known bucket path). TF output returns provenance_blob_url.

Airgap/OCI mirror considerations:
- Mirror must preserve digests and push signature artifacts (cosign signatures) and the provenance index. If a mirror cannot store signatures, enforce a local attestation file and verification step in pre-sync.
- For customers with no outbound connectivity, we push a signed bundle via secure transfer (scp/usb-certified image bundle), and the operator reads local provenance.

ArgoCD + Helm upgrade gating pattern:
- ArgoCD apps use "pre-sync" Lua hooks (or init containers) to fetch the module TF outputs (artifact_digest, provenence_blob_url) and verify signatures via cosign before applying Helm charts.
- Use a small policy-engine container (OPA/Rego) that evaluates: "is signature valid? does preflight_checksum match? is rollout policy satisfied?" If any check fails, pre-sync should exit non-zero to block the sync.
- Embed a deterministic Helm values hash into the ArgoCD App label (app.kubernetes.io/values-hash) so that drift detection becomes straightforward.

Release phases (operationally actionable):
- Phase 0: Preflight (TF plan applied in "preview" mode, preflight checks run, smoke manifests rendered and hashed).
- Phase 1: Publish artifacts (push images, push provenance index, update TF inputs or module registry artifacts).
- Phase 2: Staged sync (ArgoCD applies non-critical components, operator pods scaled with replicas=1, feature-flag off). Run health checks for 10–30 minutes or X requests.
- Phase 3: Canary/validation (increment traffic via service mesh weights or increase replicas to half of target). Run regression/eval prompt set or end-to-end smoke tests.
- Phase 4: Promote (full scale up, run longer-term health checks, finalize rollout_id -> stable in TF outputs).
- Phase 5: Finalize (record final provenance, mark release in registry index and internal tracker).

Rollback guidance:
- Keep previous artifact digests and TF state for at least N releases (configurable; recommend 7).
- Rollback is a pod/Helm/ArgoCD sync to previous manifests + TF run that restores any infra-level changes. Use the rollout_id to coordinate.
- For DB migrations: prefer idempotent forward-safe migrations; when not possible, snapshot and include snapshot_id in TF outputs to enable rollback restore.

Preflight checklist (quick actionable tasks):
- [ ] Confirm cosign signatures present for each image digest
- [ ] Verify provenance index URL reachable and signed
- [ ] Confirm TF plan shows only expected changes
- [ ] Run manifest-render dry-run and compute preflight_checksum
- [ ] Validate ArgoCD pre-sync policy/OPA tests locally
- [ ] Confirm registry mirror has artifacts and signatures (airgap: verify local bundle)
- [ ] Smoke test ingress and auth flows in staging cluster

Observability & release signals:
- Primary signals: pod restart rate, 5xx per minute, tail latency P99, token-cost delta (for LLM-serving pods), KV-cache hit ratio for models.
- Define a short list of pass/fail gates for canary: no >= 5xx spike, latency change < +25% at P99, correctness eval pass-rate > 95% on synthetic checks.
- Hook metrics into rollout controller that can auto-pause if a threshold breaches for > 3 consecutive minutes.

Operational notes / edge cases:
- If KMS key rotation occurs during a rollout, ensure the signature verification path supports key metadata lookups for historical keys. Store key metadata in the provenance bundle.
- When switching registries (e.g., from Redwood-managed to customer-managed mirror), mandate a one-off "prove-and-copy" operation that verifies digests and re-signs or copies signatures accordingly.

Open items / TODOs:
- Define exact TF output naming conventions across modules (narrow variance).
- Add a lightweight CLI utility for customers that verifies provenance index and cosign signatures in airgapped installs.
- Prototype ArgoCD pre-sync OPA policy templates for our most common patterns.
- Run a game day to practice rollback with a DB migration present.

Contacts / escalation path:
- Primary: Ethan Chen (eng-private-deployments) – ethan.chen@redwood.com
- Secondary: Priya Nair (solutions eng) – priya.nair@redwood.com
- Release support: releases@redwood.com, Slack channel #private-deploy-release

Appendix — example provenance index JSON (short form) (store this as a sidecar file in registry/S3):
{"tag":"v2.3.4","digest":"sha256:abcd...","signed_by":"projects/redwood/kms/keys/rdw-release-key","cosign_sig":"base64...","sbom_url":"s3://rdw-provenance/v2.3.4/sbom.json","build_git_sha":"f7a1c9"}

End notes: This doc is intentionally prescriptive but pragmatic. Aim is to reduce surprise during private upgrades: make artifacts verifiable, modules contract-driven, and ArgoCD pre-sync policies the gate that keeps clusters consistent. Feedback welcome — will iterate into a formal runbook after two customer pilots.
